answer:
Use the Weave agent tracing helpers. Open one `weave.start_conversation()`, then wrap each turn, LLM call and tool call in `weave.start_turn()`, `weave.start_llm()` and `weave.start_tool()`. In Python all four work as context managers [S1]. Weave groups the turns into one conversation. It does not merge them into one trace.

**Setup**
- Install `weave` and call `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")` before any `start_*` call [S3].
- If `weave.init()` is missing, the tracing functions silently do nothing [S3].

**How the pieces map**

| Your code | Weave call | OTel span |
|---|---|---|
| Whole conversation | `start_conversation(...)` | none (groups turns) |
| One user message and the agent's reply | `start_turn(...)` | `invoke_agent` |
| One model API call | `start_llm(...)` | `chat` |
| One tool execution | `start_tool(...)` | `execute_tool` |

[S1]

**How turns are linked**
- `start_conversation()` stamps a `conversation_id` on every child span. That ID is how the Agents tab groups turns [S5].
- A conversation has no parent span. Each turn's `invoke_agent` span is the root of its own OTel trace, and the shared `conversation_id` ties the turns together [S7].
- LLM and tool spans nest under their turn [S4].
- `start_turn()` takes the active conversation from context. With no active conversation, the turn isn't grouped with others [S6].
- To add turns to an existing conversation, pass the same stable `conversation_id` [S5].

**Minimal sketch.** `call_model` and `run_tool` are placeholders for your own code, and this sketch has not been run. It follows the quickstart's pattern: a first LLM call, tool calls, then a second LLM call that produces the final answer [S4].
```python
import weave
weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

def run_turn(history, user_message):
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})
    with weave.start_turn(user_message=user_message, model="gpt-4o-mini"):
        # LLM call 1: the model may request tools
        with weave.start_llm(model="gpt-4o-mini", provider_name="openai") as llm:
            msg = call_model(history)              # placeholder
            llm.output(msg.content or "")
            history.append(msg)
        if not msg.tool_calls:
            return msg.content
        for tc in msg.tool_calls:
            with weave.start_tool(name=tc.name, arguments=tc.args, tool_call_id=tc.id) as tool:
                tool.result = run_tool(tc)         # placeholder
                history.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": tc.id, "content": tool.result})
        # LLM call 2: send tool results back for the final answer
        with weave.start_llm(model="gpt-4o-mini", provider_name="openai") as llm:
            final = call_model(history)            # placeholder
            llm.output(final.content)
            history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": final.content})
            return final.content

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent"):
    history = []
    for q in ["Question 1", "Question 2"]:
        run_turn(history, q)
```
The tracing calls don't carry your dialogue, so you still keep and resend the `history` list yourself [S4].

**Optional extras**
- In the quickstart, `llm.record(usage=weave.Usage(...), response_id=..., response_model=...)` sets usage, the priced model and the response id in one call [S4].
- `agent_name` identifies the agent in the UI. Without it, the conversation isn't grouped under a named agent [S5].

## How the Weave SDK works with agents

The Weave SDK includes a generic OTel ingest system for agents, meaning that Weave can capture information from any OTel span in your agent's code. However, Weave requires special handling of the following spans to render your agent's traces in the Agents view of the Weights & Biases UI.

| Concept | Python | TypeScript | OTel span |
| - | - | - | - |
| A conversation | `weave.start_conversation(...)` | `weave.startConversation(...)` | (no span, groups turns) |
| One user or agent exchange | `weave.start_turn(...)` | `weave.startTurn(...)` | `invoke_agent` |
| One LLM API call | `weave.start_llm(...)` | `weave.startLLM(...)` | `chat` |
| One tool execution | `weave.start_tool(...)` | `weave.startTool(...)` | `execute_tool` |

In Python, all four functions work as context managers (`with weave.start_*(...) as obj:`). On exit, they end the span and flush attributes, including on exceptions. In TypeScript, call `.end()` on each returned object. Use `try { ... } finally { obj.end(); }` to guarantee cleanup on exceptions.

Other [GenAI semantic-convention attributes](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans/), such as `gen_ai.usage.*` and `gen_ai.agent.name`, enable additional rendering, but they're optional.

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

agent_name"] Agent --> S1 & S2 S1["Conversation 1
conversation_id
(no OTel span)"] S2["Conversation 2
conversation_id
(no OTel span)"] S1 --> T1 & T2 S2 --> T3 T1["Turn 1
invoke_agent
(root span, own trace)"] T2["Turn 2
invoke_agent
(root span, own trace)"] T3["Turn 1
invoke_agent
(root span, own trace)"] T1 --> L1 & L2 L1["LLM call
chat"] L2["LLM call
chat"] L1 --> Tool1["Tool call
execute_tool"] classDef agent fill:#DE72FF33,stroke:#454B52,stroke-width:2px classDef conversation fill:#FFD95C33,stroke:#454B52,stroke-width:2px classDef turn fill:#00CDDB33,stroke:#454B52,stroke-width:2px classDef llm fill:#FFCBAD33,stroke:#454B52,stroke-width:2px classDef tool fill:#f4f4f5,stroke:#454B52,stroke-width:2px class Agent agent class S1,S2 conversation class T1,T2,T3 turn class L1,L2 llm class Tool1 tool ``` A conversation groups turns by a shared `conversation_id` attribute rather than a parent span, so each turn starts its own OTel trace. ## How the Weave SDK works with agents

The Weave SDK includes a generic OTel ingest system for agents, meaning that Weave can capture information from any OTel span in your agent's code. However, Weave requires special handling of the following spans to render your agent's traces in the Agents view of the Weights & Biases UI.

| Concept | Python | TypeScript | OTel span |
| - | - | - | - |
| A conversation | `weave.start_conversation(...)` | `weave.startConversation(...)` | (no span, groups turns) |
| One user or agent exchange | `weave.start_turn(...)` | `weave.startTurn(...)` | `invoke_agent` |
| One LLM API call | `weave.start_llm(...)` | `weave.startLLM(...)` | `chat` |
| One tool execution | `weave.start_tool(...)` | `weave.startTool(...)` | `execute_tool` |

In Python, all four functions work as context managers (`with weave.start_*(...) as obj:`). On exit, they end the span and flush attributes, including on exceptions. In TypeScript, call `.end()` on each returned object. Use `try { ... } finally { obj.end(); }` to guarantee cleanup on exceptions.

Other [GenAI semantic-convention attributes](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans/), such as `gen_ai.usage.*` and `gen_ai.agent.name`, enable additional rendering, but they're optional.

result.text:
## How the Weave SDK works with agents

The Weave SDK includes a generic OTel ingest system for agents, meaning that Weave can capture information from any OTel span in your agent's code. However, Weave requires special handling of the following spans to render your agent's traces in the Agents view of the Weights & Biases UI.

| Concept | Python | TypeScript | OTel span |
| - | - | - | - |
| A conversation | `weave.start_conversation(...)` | `weave.startConversation(...)` | (no span, groups turns) |
| One user or agent exchange | `weave.start_turn(...)` | `weave.startTurn(...)` | `invoke_agent` |
| One LLM API call | `weave.start_llm(...)` | `weave.startLLM(...)` | `chat` |
| One tool execution | `weave.start_tool(...)` | `weave.startTool(...)` | `execute_tool` |

In Python, all four functions work as context managers (`with weave.start_*(...) as obj:`). On exit, they end the span and flush attributes, including on exceptions. In TypeScript, call `.end()` on each returned object. Use `try { ... } finally { obj.end(); }` to guarantee cleanup on exceptions.

Other [GenAI semantic-convention attributes](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans/), such as `gen_ai.usage.*` and `gen_ai.agent.name`, enable additional rendering, but they're optional.

# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

agent_name"] Agent --> S1 & S2 S1["Conversation 1
conversation_id
(no OTel span)"] S2["Conversation 2
conversation_id
(no OTel span)"] S1 --> T1 & T2 S2 --> T3 T1["Turn 1
invoke_agent
(root span, own trace)"] T2["Turn 2
invoke_agent
(root span, own trace)"] T3["Turn 1
invoke_agent
(root span, own trace)"] T1 --> L1 & L2 L1["LLM call
chat"] L2["LLM call
chat"] L1 --> Tool1["Tool call
execute_tool"] classDef agent fill:#DE72FF33,stroke:#454B52,stroke-width:2px classDef conversation fill:#FFD95C33,stroke:#454B52,stroke-width:2px classDef turn fill:#00CDDB33,stroke:#454B52,stroke-width:2px classDef llm fill:#FFCBAD33,stroke:#454B52,stroke-width:2px classDef tool fill:#f4f4f5,stroke:#454B52,stroke-width:2px class Agent agent class S1,S2 conversation class T1,T2,T3 turn class L1,L2 llm class Tool1 tool ``` A conversation groups turns by a shared `conversation_id` attribute rather than a parent span, so each turn starts its own OTel trace. This design supports distributed tracing and parallel execution. The client sends spans directly to the OTel collector without any server-side aggregation. > [!TIP] > > To integrate Weave with SDKs or harnesses such as the Claude Agent SDK or Codex, see [Choose an agent integration](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/agent-integration-quickstart.md). Weave autopatches into several agent-building SDKs and agent harnesses for quick integration. Those integrations set `conversation_id` from the SDK or harness session, so you don't need `start_conversation()` to group their turns. The APIs on this page are for agents you instrument yourself.

Use the Weave agent tracing helpers. Open one `weave.start_conversation()`, then wrap each turn, LLM call and tool call in `weave.start_turn()`, `weave.start_llm()` and `weave.start_tool()`. In Python all four work as context managers [S1]. Weave groups the turns into one conversation. It does not merge them into one trace.

**Setup**
- Install `weave` and call `weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")` before any `start_*` call [S3].
- If `weave.init()` is missing, the tracing functions silently do nothing [S3].

**How the pieces map**

| Your code | Weave call | OTel span |
|---|---|---|
| Whole conversation | `start_conversation(...)` | none (groups turns) |
| One user message and the agent's reply | `start_turn(...)` | `invoke_agent` |
| One model API call | `start_llm(...)` | `chat` |
| One tool execution | `start_tool(...)` | `execute_tool` |

[S1]

**How turns are linked**
- `start_conversation()` stamps a `conversation_id` on every child span. That ID is how the Agents tab groups turns [S5].
- A conversation has no parent span. Each turn's `invoke_agent` span is the root of its own OTel trace, and the shared `conversation_id` ties the turns together [S7].
- LLM and tool spans nest under their turn [S4].
- `start_turn()` takes the active conversation from context. With no active conversation, the turn isn't grouped with others [S6].
- To add turns to an existing conversation, pass the same stable `conversation_id` [S5].

**Minimal sketch.** `call_model` and `run_tool` are placeholders for your own code. This is not a tested run.
```python
import weave
weave.init("[YOUR-TEAM]/[YOUR-PROJECT]")

def run_turn(history, user_message):
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})
    with weave.start_turn(user_message=user_message, model="gpt-4o-mini"):
        with weave.start_llm(model="gpt-4o-mini", provider_name="openai") as llm:
            msg = call_model(history)          # placeholder
            llm.output(msg.content or "")
            history.append(msg)
        for tc in msg.tool_calls or []:
            with weave.start_tool(name=tc.name, arguments=tc.args, tool_call_id=tc.id) as tool:
                tool.result = run_tool(tc)     # placeholder
                history.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": tc.id, "content": tool.result})
        # ...a second LLM call would produce the final answer
    return msg.content

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="my-agent"):
    history = []
    for q in ["Question 1", "Question 2"]:
        run_turn(history, q)
```
The structure follows the quickstart's three-turn agent loop [S4]. The tracing calls don't carry your dialogue, so you still keep and resend the `history` list yourself [S4].

**Optional extras**
- Record token usage with `llm.record(usage=weave.Usage(...), response_id=..., response_model=...)` so token counts and cost render [S4].
- `agent_name` makes the conversation appear under a named agent in the UI. Without it, the conversation isn't grouped under one [S5].
